metadata.title: Why the Server Hands Back an Encrypted Context You're Only Going to Echo
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: why does compaction hand back an encrypted blob you're only going to echo? Lands the carry-out that the readable summary is for you, the encrypted blob is what actually carries the conversation's memory forward.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B04 (twenty-turn compaction case, paid off with the blob passed forward instead of a message replay)

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes the readable summary Claude hands back is what it remembers. It's not — it's just what's shown to you. So why does the server hand back an encrypted blob you're only going to echo?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'The summary is what Claude remembers, right?', hesitates on 'remembers', corrects to 'shows you', lands the real question

props.text:
The summary is what
Claude remembers, right?
So why does passing it
back lose the context?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('remembers' -> 'shows you') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: When a chat gets long, compaction fires and hands you back two things: a readable summary, and an opaque encrypted blob. The natural guess is that the summary — the part you can read — is what carries the memory forward. Pass it alone into the next call, and the context breaks anyway.

shot.new_visual_element: A tall message stack branching into two outputs; the readable-summary path dead-ends

production_viz.label: Two outputs, one dead end
production_viz.mechanic: A tall stack of message bubbles labelled 'LONG CHAT' on cream. It branches into two paths: 'READABLE SUMMARY' (thin, ink only) heading toward 'NEXT CALL' but stopping short with a break mark; 'ENCRYPTED BLOB' (solid card, terracotta border) continuing unbroken toward 'NEXT CALL'.

beats.narration_text: Here's the concrete case. A twenty-turn conversation overflows, and compaction fires. You get back content: "Earlier conversation summarized" in plain English, right next to encrypted_content: a sealed string starting "EpwBCioIDxgC…". Thread the readable text into the next call, and context breaks. Thread the blob back instead, and it holds.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR - the stack collapsing into an open speech bubble and a sealed box; only the box's path continues

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR - collapse into two outputs, one path holds
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. A tall stack of twenty message bubbles collapses into one block, which emits two shapes: an open speech bubble labelled 'content: "Earlier conversation summarized"' and a sealed box labelled 'encrypted_content: "EpwBCioIDxgC..."' with a terracotta border. An arrow from the speech bubble toward 'NEXT CALL' breaks with an X; the arrow from the sealed box reaches 'NEXT CALL' intact. THIS COLLAPSE COMPOSITION RETURNS AT B04.

beats.narration_text: Here's why. The readable text is display and debug only — it's for you, not for the model. The encrypted blob is a server-verifiable token: it reconstructs the full compressed context — turn boundaries, roles, metadata — everything the plain summary throws away.

shot.new_visual_element: Speech bubble labelled 'display only'; sealed box unpacking into turn boundaries / roles / metadata

production_viz.label: Display text vs. server-verifiable token
production_viz.mechanic: Left: the open speech bubble from B02, labelled underneath 'DISPLAY / DEBUG ONLY' in ink. Right: the sealed box, terracotta border, unpacking (arrows fanning out) into three labelled fields: 'turn boundaries', 'roles', 'metadata'. Beneath the speech bubble, the same three field labels appear crossed out in ink, captioned 'thrown away'.

beats.narration_text: So on the next call, you pass only the blob. The server doesn't replay twenty messages — it rebuilds the full context straight from the token. Passing the blob restores everything compaction saved; it doesn't make the readable summary useless, since that text is still exactly what you'd show a user or a log.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS - 20 messages crossed out, replaced by one token; the speech bubble persists, labelled still useful

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS - one token, not a replay
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 COLLAPSE COMPOSITION RETURNS: the twenty-message stack now shown crossed out in ink beside a single sealed box (terracotta border) with an unbroken arrow to 'NEXT CALL'. Off to the side, the open speech bubble from B02/B03 persists, unbroken, captioned 'still useful — for display' in ink (no accent — it is not the thing that failed).

beats.narration_text: The readable summary is for your eyes; the encrypted blob is what actually carries the conversation's memory forward.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. You're building a multi-turn PHP app with the Anthropic SDK. Show me how to detect a compaction block in the response, and write the code that threads the encrypted_content blob — not the human-readable summary — back into the next messages array. Explain what breaks if you send the summary text instead. Liam, in for Bear.
